findings.closure_evidence: Recorder now starts the direct launcher child with start_new_session=True, records launcher_session_isolated, and wraps post-spawn event writes plus wait in the KeyboardInterrupt path. The handler forwards SIGINT only through the still-owned Popen handle and waits for that handle. The new non-MPI test isolates the recorder group, checks the child receives exactly one forwarded SIGINT, and verifies the child's exit code 7 remains the recorded and CLI status.
findings.residual_limit: The recorder does not promise cleanup of descendants or process-group emptiness, and docs now limit the path to the noninteractive native case; this is consistent with the owned-direct-child contract.

contract_review.interrupt_and_status: Static review confirms session isolation prevents terminal Ctrl-C from directly reaching the launcher before forwarding. Popen.wait remains the source of launcher_return_code; trace text does not convert a nonzero or signaled exit into success.
contract_review.mpi_abi_and_forwarding: The C adapter now statically requires 32-bit int and MPI_Fint, matching its documented registered GNU Fortran/Open MPI ABI. mpi_init_ and mpi_finalize_ pass the original ierr pointer once to their PMPI counterparts; tracing preserves errno and does not synthesize or rewrite ierr. Root reports compilation against installed Open MPI headers and nm showing only PMPI lifecycle imports; this reviewer did not repeat that compile.
contract_review.fortran_instrumentation: All inserted calls remain behind WRF_NATIVE_EXIT_TRACE. Existing wrf_dm_shutdown remains the MPI_Finalize owner. The test's hash-based preprocessed default-off oracle is shallow-clone friendly; actual shutdown-body oracle tests phase ordering with fake PMPI, without an MPI launch.
contract_review.thread_semantics: Docs distinguish MPI_THREAD_SINGLE from MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED and state that the pthread token does not establish the provided MPI level. Python native thread IDs and C pthread tokens are separate identity domains; monotonic samples are also explicitly documented as separate clock domains.
contract_review.ci_scope: CI adds only the existing non-MPI core job's fake-PMPI/source-oracle test invocation and installs gfortran for the extracted Fortran oracle. No WRF/MPI/PMIx launch is added.
contract_review.frozen_artifacts: The frozen native_twin_runner.py is unchanged in the worktree status; no change to the frozen execution path or source artifact bindings was observed.

root_cause_and_gates.historical_2RC1_cause: unknown; this implementation does not establish attribution
root_cause_and_gates.additional_mpi_lifecycle_or_thread_queri: none added beyond forwarding the existing F77 MPI_Init/MPI_Finalize calls

validation.this_review: Read-only source/diff review and git diff --check only; no tests, MPI/PMIx/WRF launches, or production changes.
validation.reported_by_root_not_independently_repea: Five local non-MPI tests passed, including the Fortran source oracle and default-off preprocessing; actual Open MPI header compile and symbol inspection passed.

conclusion: The previously reported interrupt-delivery issue is closed by session isolation plus direct-child signal forwarding, with a targeted fake-child regression test. No remaining actionable defect found in the reviewed diagnostic change. Full WRF rebuild/deployment behavior remains unverified, as documented.

portability_delta_review.change: The C observer defines _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L before all headers when the caller has not defined it; the fake C test compile no longer supplies the macro on its command line.
portability_delta_review.impact: This makes clock_gettime/POSIX declarations self-contained for the tested C11 compile. No control flow, symbols, lifecycle calls, status handling, or Fortran instrumentation changed in this delta.
portability_delta_review.tests: Root reports all five non-MPI tests and the actual Open MPI header compile were rerun after this delta; not independently rerun in this static review.
